We have tried many weighted full, weighted pool4 inverse, softmax, etc. We haven't tried mean on pool4 (F) or trimmed_mean on pool4 (G). Also dba on pool4 (D). Let's choose mean on pool4 to see if smaller pool better.

attempts.rationale: The series has strong trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a simple robust median may handle outliers and correlated errors.
The series has unstable ranking and several correlated error groups; a weighted inverse error might exploit relative performance while avoiding overfitting.
try a DBA combination, a robust alternative to median/mean that may handle correlated errors.
test a weighted combo with softmax_neg_error on the full pool to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over inverse_error and median.
test a simple mean combination over the full pool, as a different kind of aggregate to compare against robust methods.
Test a per‑horizon best‑model weighting (best_per_horizon) on the full pool to see if horizon‑specific gains improve over robust aggregates, given the unstable ranking and high outlier rate.
test a weighted combination that focuses on the most stable, low-error models (pool4) with inverse_error weights to see if a more selective weighted mean beats the robust median.
Test a trimmed mean on the full pool to see if excluding extremes improves robustness given high outlier pct and unstable ranking.
Test a robust median on the reduced, diversified pool4 to see if trimming outliers improves over full‑pool median, given strong trend/seasonality and unstable ranking.
test a per‑horizon top‑k mean weighting on the full pool to see if horizon‑specific averaging improves over global weights.
try a per‑horizon softmax weighting on the smaller, more diverse pool4 to capture horizon‑specific strengths while keeping robustness.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9043. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.045); 9 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 2.362.
